Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.

# Summary of 2024 General Election Manifesto

This manifesto addresses what it identifies as interconnected crises: cost of living pressures, climate emergency, and declining public services. It argues that solutions to environmental challenges simultaneously address economic inequality and service provision.

## Healthcare and Social Care

The document proposes significant NHS investment, including £28bn additional annual expenditure by 2030 and £20bn capital spending over five years. Key commitments include reducing waiting lists, guaranteeing GP access, universal NHS dentistry access (£3bn annually by 2030), and staff pay increases. Mental health services would receive equal priority to physical health, with 28-day access targets for therapies.

Social care would receive £20bn annually, introducing free personal care modelled on Scottish provision, alongside improved pay and career structures for care workers.

## Housing

The manifesto proposes 150,000 new social homes annually, ending right-to-buy, empowering local authorities to implement rent controls, and ending no-fault evictions. A major retrofit programme (£29bn over five years) would insulate homes to high standards, reducing energy bills and emissions.

## Energy and Environment

The document advocates transitioning to renewable energy, with wind providing approximately 70% of electricity by 2030. It opposes new fossil fuel extraction and nuclear power development, proposing community ownership of energy infrastructure and public ownership of major energy companies.

Environmental commitments include 30% of land and seas protected for nature by 2030, water company renationalisation, a Rights of Nature Act, and significant investment in habitat restoration.

## Economy and Taxation

Economic proposals include £40bn average annual green investment, public ownership of railways and utilities, and a carbon tax starting at £120 per tonne. Revenue would come from wealth taxes on assets exceeding £10m, aligned capital gains and income tax rates, and reformed inheritance tax—estimated to raise £50-70bn annually.

## Education and Transport

Education proposals include ending tuition fees, restoring maintenance grants, £8bn school investment, and £5bn for special educational needs. Transport investment totals £19bn over five years, prioritising public transport, rail renationalisation, cycling infrastructure, and phasing out petrol/diesel vehicles by 2035.

## Democracy and International Affairs

Democratic reforms include proportional representation, votes at 16, and House of Lords replacement. International commitments include restoring overseas aid to 0.7% of GNI (rising to 1%), supporting international law enforcement, and working toward EU membership.
